title: What is known about 1RB1LF_0LC0RE_1LA1RD_0LB1LB_1RC1RD_0LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LF_0LC0RE_1LA1RD_0LB1LB_1RC1RD_0LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape's words are identified; no macro rule is known yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 21,829 cells have been visited and 14,286 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.497). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.112).

claims.title: What the tape is made of
claims.text: Mostly the word 110, in a few long runs separated by markers (11110, 1111110, 00 …); the runs exchange length from sweep to sweep.

claims.title: Shift rules, for any number of copies
claims.text: C runs right over runs of 110 (turning them into 001) and of 10, D runs left over 100 (into 011); each for every number of copies and any tape around.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when C reads a 0 with two 1s to its left; whether the markers ever produce that is open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine fills its tape with the word 110, in a few long runs separated by small markers that move and change. This page runs the real machine and shows what its tape is made of.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
The word most of the tape is made of.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.497). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.112).
After 109 steps the tape spans 21,829 cells (16,661 left of the start, 114 right), with a density of 1s of 0.654.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Runs of 110 and markers
html: Each time the head is at the left end in state B, the tape is a short prefix and then a few long runs of b = 110 separated by markers:

The runs swap length from sweep to sweep while the markers move, appear and vanish. The machine halts exactly when it is in state C on a 0 with two 1s to its left; inside the runs of 110 every 0 has that shape, so the markers decide. No regular round has been isolated yet.

summary: A few long runs of 110 separated by short markers that swap material from sweep to sweep; no regular round isolated yet; halts exactly at 1 1 C>0.
